title: Bix lends him money at a Park Avenue party
summary: Out of work between Pollack engagements he asks Bix for money and gets $200.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: Now that we've just listened to Bix has stirred this up some more memories?

Yes it has Helen. He was quite a human being this guy. I recall once again in New York City with Ben Pollack's band and between the Little Club and the Park Central Hotel we were off about six or seven weeks. Because Ben Pollack quit the 'Little Club', and no work. So there used to be a place called Jimmy Plunkett's. It was a speak easy on 53rd Street between 7th and Broadway. And that's where all the jazz musicians or the musicians around town, with Jimmy, Tommy Dorsey, Goodman, Bix and all the Whiteman band, oh so many guys used to congregate there. It was our water hole so to speak. It was a speak easy.

And I recall one day Bix, well no, this is when he, that's right, I'm going a little ahead of my story. I'm inbetween the jobs at the Little Club and the Park Central Hotel which I believe was around 1929.

We were invited to go into parties you know. Musicians, like a big Park Avenue party and some of these people with lots of money and you know, come and bring your horn, style. So we said, well let's go you know. So we did, the Pollack band. So we got there and the Whiteman band was there also. With Bix Beiderbecke and Trumbauer, the Dorsey brothers Jimmy and Tommy Dorsey and the Pollack band was there with Benny Goodman, and Jack Teagarden ......
Can't (hear that?) for a few drinks and some food huh? (LAUGHTER). I mean, what the host got, yes.

That's the bad part of it. There was no food. They had plenty of drinks, they had plenty of drinks, all the drinks you want and we're starving to death. I mean us guys in the Pollack band because we didn't have any money. We were inbetween jobs you know. You spend all your money when you're working.

So we get there and here's Bix and we played and everything, we had a few drinks and were playing. And I called Bix, I said I wanted to talk to him. I said I want to talk to you Bix, you know. So I told him,

look Bix, we're out of work and man I haven't got any money to buy food, you know, we haven't got a job. He said, well how much do you need? I said, all I need is five bucks, ten bucks and I'll pay you next....... He says, come on, really, so he pulled out four fifty dollar bills and gave me two hundred dollars.

I said, I don't need two hundred dollars Bix, I just, ten bucks is enough. He says, kid, take the money, I've got plenty of money, we're working. He says, when you get it you pay me back you know. He finally forced it on me and gave me the money. Alright, I paid him back after we started working at the Park Central Hotel making a lot of money. $650 a week, $650 a week.
